[[File: Jean-Benoit Bost.jpg | thumb|Jean-Benoit Bost, [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics|Oberwolfach]] 2005]]
'''Jean-Benoît Bost''' (born 27 July 1961, in [[Neuilly-sur-Seine]]) is a French mathematician.

==Early life and education==
In 1977, Bost graduated from the [[Lycée Louis-le-Grand]] and finished first in the [[Concours général]], a national competition. Bost studied from 1979 to 1983 (qualifying in 1981 for the ''agrégation des mathématiques'') at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] (ENS), where he was from 1984 to 1988 ''[[Agrégation|agrégé]]-préparateur'' (teacher) and worked under the direction of [[Alain Connes]].

==Career==
From 1988, Bost was ''chargé de recherches'' and from 1993 ''directeur de recherches'' at the [[National Center for Scientific Research|Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS)]]. From 1993 to 2006, he was ''maître de conferences'' at the [[École polytechnique]]. He has been a professor at l'[[Université Paris-Saclay]] (Paris XI) in [[Orsay]] since 1998.

==Research==
Bost deals with [[noncommutative geometry]] (partly in collaboration with [[Alain Connes]]) with applications to [[quantum field theory]], [[algebraic geometry]], and [[arithmetic geometry]]. The eponymous [[Farrell-Jones conjecture#Bost conjecture|Bost conjecture]] is a variant of the [[Baum–Connes conjecture]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Bartels, Arthur|author-link=Arthur Bartels|author2=Echterhoff, Siegfried|author3=Lück, Wolfgang|author-link3=Wolfgang Lück|title=Inheritance of Isomorphism Conjectures under colimits|year=2007|eprint=math/0702460 }}</ref>

His work with François Charles on Archimedean overflow<ref>{{citation | last1=Bost | first1=Jean-Benoît | last2=Charles | first2=François | title=Quasi-projective and formal-analytic arithmetic surfaces | date=2022 | arxiv=2206.14242 | url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.14242 | access-date=2025-12-19 | page=}}</ref> generalizes the arithmetic holonomicity theorem of [[Frank Calegari|Calegari]]-Dimitrov-[[Yunqing Tang|Tang]].<ref name= "UnboundedDenominators">{{cite arXiv |eprint=2109.09040 |last1=Calegari |first1=Frank |last2=Dimitrov |first2=Vesselin |last3=Tang |first3=Yunqing |title=The Unbounded Denominators Conjecture |date=2021 |class=math.NT }}</ref> It also establishes an arithmetic counterpart of theorems of Lefschetz and [[Madhav V. Nori|Nori]] on fundamental groups of complex surfaces.

==Awards and honors==
In 1990, he received the Prix Peccot-Vimont of the [[Collège de France]]. In 2002, he received the [[Elie Cartan Prize|Prix Élie Cartan]] of the [[Académie des sciences]]. In 1986 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress on Mathematical Physics]] in [[Marseille]].<ref>{{cite book | editor-last1=Mebkhout | editor-first1=M. | editor-last2=Sénéor | editor-first2=R. | title=VIIIth International Congress on Mathematical Physics | publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company | date=1987 | isbn=978-9971-5-0208-9 | chapter=Conformal and holomorphic anomalies on riemann surfaces and determinant line bundles | author-last=Bost | author-first=Jean-Benoît }}</ref> In 2006, he was an invited speaker with talk ''Evaluation maps, slopes, and algebraicity criteria'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Madrid]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Bost, Jean-Benoît|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Madrid, 2006|chapter=Evaluation maps, slopes, and algebraicity conjectures|volume=2|pages=537–562|publisher=European Mathematical Society}}</ref>

From 2005 to 2015, Bost was a senior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]]. He was elected in 2012 a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and in 2016 a member of [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jean-Benoît Bost|website=Academia Europaea|url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Bost_Jean-Benoît}}</ref>
